name: Iran nuclear programme
value: No IAEA access; Iran rejects inspections 14 Nov
summary: IAEA says it cannot verify Iran's near-weapons-grade uranium; Iran says inspections cannot resume during the war
state: An IAEA report circulated on 13 Nov said the gap in information on Iran's near-weapons-grade uranium stockpile is a proliferation concern needing urgent action, and that inspectors do not know the status of the declared Isfahan enrichment plant (Al Jazeera). On 14 Nov Iran's mission in Vienna called IAEA Board resolutions legally flawed and said normal inspections cannot resume while its sites are under attack (Tasnim). No new strike on a nuclear site, NPT withdrawal or evidence of weaponisation was found as of 17 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: No direct effect on daily life. Loss of inspection access adds uncertainty about Iran's programme and the risk of further military action in the Gulf, which can feed through to energy prices and regional travel.
rubric_hit: Inspector access curtailed: IAEA cannot verify Iran's enriched uranium stockpile (report 13 Nov) = Watch

why: A nuclear-armed Iran — or strikes to prevent one — could ignite the Gulf and send oil far higher.
drivers: Enrichment levels, IAEA access, Israeli/US military posture, snapback sanctions, talks.

rubric.alert: Strikes on nuclear sites, NPT withdrawal, or evidence of weaponisation.
rubric.watch: Enrichment at ≥ 60% or inspector access curtailed, or credible strike threats.
rubric.normal: IAEA access and active diplomacy; no escalation.
